title: Kiosk Navigation: telemetry-first console prototype for role-scoped sidebar & lightweight workspace switching
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Product and platform teams need a fast, low-noise way to switch contexts in the Redwood Console when responding to alerts, inspecting rollout health, or triaging cost spikes. Current workspace switching and sidebar patterns surface too much information for rapid tasks and obscure telemetry relevant to on-call and SRE flows.

Goal: Ship a lightweight 'kiosk' navigation mode and role-scoped sidebar configuration that surfaces targeted telemetry tiles (rollout health, token-cost delta, latency hotspots), reduces click-depth for common triage flows, and preserves full console navigation for power users. The design should be accessible, performant, and compatible with dedicated/private deployment variants.

Proposed solution:
- Introduce a collapsible Kiosk Rail: a slim, single-column rail that replaces the full left rail when users opt into a compact/incident persona. Rail items are prioritized by recent alerts and owned services.
- Role-scoped lanes: a mapping between user role (on-call, billing, infra) and sidebar lanes to surface role-relevant dashboards, rollout controls, and cost lenses.
- Workspace Snapshots: ephemeral, lightweight workspace states that persist a pinned model/version + route and can be switched to from the kiosk rail in one click. Snapshots load progressively (telemetry tiles first).
- Telemetry-first tiles: small-card components with pre-cached KPIs (SLO%, 99th latency, cost delta) that hydrate in under 150ms for the common case.
- Quick actions: inline rollout pause/rollback, reroute requests, and toast-driven fallback suggestions available from the kiosk rail without full route transitions.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Prototype demonstrates sub-150ms first-tile paint in lab environment; 2) Participants in usability test (N=6) can complete three triage tasks 25% faster than baseline; 3) Engineering review confirms no major routing/ACL blockers for Private deployments; 4) Design signoff and accessible keyboard/ARIA patterns documented.
